title: Stratified runtime sampling + prefetch attribution instrumentation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: provide a low-overhead, stratified sampling and instrumentation surface that attributes per-token latency and unit cost to runtime phases (prefill/prefetch, kv-cache hit/miss, emission) so PM/infra can correlate cache behavior with per-token cost and downstream SLOs.

Background: We currently surface request-level latencies and have token slicing traces in a few places, but we lack a production-safe, sampled stream that ties token emission timing to upstream KV cache behavior, prefetch work, and scheduling delays inside the serving runtime. Without this we cannot quantify the cost benefit of prefetch strategies or the true latency penalty of cache misses for different sequence positions and batch shapes.

Scope: implement lightweight tracing hooks in the runtime to emit token-level probe events with minimal overhead; design a stratified sampling strategy so we record full per-token spans for a small fraction of requests while emitting aggregated metrics for all requests; add attributes to indicate cache_tier, kv_hit (true/false), prefetch_trigger (true/false), batch_size_bucket, sequence_position, model_variant, and fallback_route. Build an ingestion transformer to reconstruct token timelines from sampled spans, produce token-level histograms and eviction-sensitive delta metrics, and expose dashboard panels showing cost-per-token, median/95/99 latency contribution by cache_hit, and prefetch ROI by workload.

Non-goals: full sampling of every token for every request (too expensive), changing runtime scheduling/prefetch algorithms in this ticket (this is telemetry only), or changing billing semantics.

Design notes: runtime hooks will emit small OTLP/JSON events with 3 ms budget for emission (target additional p95 overhead < 1%). Events will be batched and pushed to an internal trace/metrics pipeline. We will include a compact token-id (hash) to allow reconstruction without storing raw user text. To reduce cardinality, tags will be enumerated (cache_tier: "L1","L2","MISS"; prefetch: "none","prefill","speculative"), and sequence_position will be coarsened into bins for aggregate metrics while raw pos is retained for sampled traces only.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits token probe spans for sampled requests with attributes: kv_hit, cache_tier, prefetch_trigger, batch_size_bucket, sequence_position_coarse, model_variant
Overall runtime overhead when sampling enabled remains < 1.2% p95 on a standard benchmark (seq_len=512, batch=8)
Ingestion pipeline reconstructs token timelines for sampled requests and produces aggregated metrics (token_latency_histogram, token_kv_miss_rate_by_pos, prefetch_latency_delta)
Grafana dashboard includes panels: per-token median/95/99 latency by kv_hit, prefetch ROI heatmap by model_variant and batch_size, and alert rule for sudden increase in token-level kv_miss_rate
Migration plan documented and feature flag exists to toggle sampling in prod per-customer / per-region
tasks: Add lightweight token probe API to runtime (C++/Rust): emit event with < 64 bytes of payload
Implement stratified sampler component in runtime: buckets by seq_len, batch_size, model_variant
Instrument KV cache layer to set kv_hit / cache_tier tags and record prefetch markers
Add telemetry exporter route to internal OTLP pipeline (trace throttling + batching)
Transformer job: reconstruct token timelines into canonical token_event rows and compute derived metrics
Create Grafana dashboard and PromQL queries / MQL equivalents
E2E performance test and canary rollout configuration behind feature flag
Docs: design spec and runbook for interpreting token-level dashboards
